CRM.rationale: CRM presents a compelling earnings-improvement-at-compressed-valuation setup. Revenue grew 13.3% YoY to $11.13B, EPS surged 52.2% to $2.42, and net margin expanded from 12.7% to 18.7% — all backed by $6.7B operating cash flow confirming cash-real earnings. The PE at 19.1x sits at the floor of its 1-year range (19.1–57.6x), with earnings yield of 5.2% exceeding the 10Y Treasury at 4.45%. The franchise is durable: 20%+ global CRM market share, 150K+ customers, 90%+ recurring revenue, and Agentforce ARR crossing $1.2B (up 205% YoY) signals a credible AI pivot. Aggressive capital returns ($25B ASR reducing share count ~10%) further support per-share value. However, the balance sheet has undergone a dramatic structural shift — debt surged from $8.44B to $39.28B (D/E from 0.14x to 1.15x), equity halved from $61.33B to $34.23B, and P/B sits at the ceiling of its range (4.48x). In a rising-rate environment (10Y at 4.45%, Baa at 6.02%), this leverage introduces meaningful refinancing and interest burden risk. Guidance was slightly soft (Q2 revenue below consensus, RPO missed by ~$700M), and management is banking on a second-half reacceleration. Tableau and Marketing/Commerce softness are real headwinds. Agentforce remains sub-5% of total revenue, so the AI transition is early. The score reflects strong Pillar 1 fundamentals (earnings acceleration, margin expansion, cash generation) and clearly attractive Pillar 2 valuation vs own history, tempered by the balance-sheet risk that caps the upside and the lack of a clear near-term catalyst beyond the earnings beat that has already been delivered. The stock's 30%+ YTD decline and three consecutive quarterly drops suggest the market is pricing in risk before proof — creating opportunity if execution continues, but the leverage makes this a qualified rather than high-conviction call.
